t: For an additional amount for “Printing and binding,” $5,295,000, fiscal year 1980: Provided, That this appropriation shall not be available for printing and binding part 2 of the Annual Report of the Secretary of Agriculture (known as the Yearbook of Agriculture): Provided further, That this appropriation shall be available for the payment of obligations incurred under the appropriations for similar purposes for preceding fiscal years.

fable.w: This section is a supplemental appropriation for printing and binding, with provisos limiting how the funds may be used. No party outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any federal decision; the reference to the Annual Report of the Secretary of Agriculture is merely a funding restriction, not a participation process.
fable.s: For an additional amount for “Printing and binding,” $5,295,000, fiscal year 1980

opus.w: This section only appropriates money for printing and binding and limits how the money can be used. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The mention of the Secretary of Agriculture's Annual Report is just a spending limit, not a process that brings outsiders into a decision.
opus.s: For an additional amount for “Printing and binding,” $5,295,000, fiscal year 1980

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriations provision that restricts the use of funds for printing a specific government report. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts) before a decision is made. The mention of the 'Annual Report' refers to the output of the agency, not a participatory process for its creation.
qwen_chat.s: For an additional amount for “Printing and binding,” $5,295,000, fiscal year 1980: Provided, That this appropriation shall not be available for printing and binding part 2 of the Annual Report of the Secretary of Agriculture (known as the Yearbook of Agriculture): Provided further, That this appropriation shall be available for the payment of obligations incurred under the appropriations for similar purposes for preceding fiscal years.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions an "Annual Report," it implies a process of gathering information from the public or other entities, thus constituting participation. However, the text itself only restricts the use of funds for printing a specific report and does not mandate any consultation, hearing, or input from outside parties. The report is an internal government document (or at least, the statute does not specify external input requirements for its creation).
